nodes.name: NF cleaning and Co coating
nodes.procedure: Nickel foams (~1 cm × 1.5 cm) were cleaned by sonicating in acetone, hydrochloric acid, and alcohol for 15 min, respectively. Next, three pieces of clean NFs were immersed into the Co(NO3)2·6H2O alcohol solution (0.2 mol·L⁻¹) for 1 min and then dried thoroughly at 60 °C. The above process was repeated 8 times.

nodes.name: NiSe@Co₀.₈₅Se/NF selenization
nodes.procedure: Anionic precursor of triethylene glycol (TEG, 40 ml) dissolved with Se powder (1.0 mmol) was stirred and heated to 270 °C in a three-necked flask fitted with a condenser pipe. Then, three pieces of coated NFs were put into the heated Se solution. After refluxing at 270 °C for 30 min, the solution was cooled to room temperature and the samples were cleaned in alcohol (99%) 3 times and dried at 60 °C.

nodes.name: Co₀.₈₅Se powder synthesis
nodes.procedure: Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.85 mmol) was added into TEG (10 ml) solution and dissolved adequately as cationic precursor. The base solution of TEG (30 ml) with Se powder (1.0 mmol) was heated to 270 °C. Then, the cationic precursor was injected into the base solution and refluxed for 30 min. The products were cleaned with alcohol at least 3 times, and then dried at 60 °C.

nodes.characterization_summary: All diffraction peaks ascribed to hexagonal NiSe (JCPDS No. 02-0892) and hexagonal close-packed Co0.85Se (JCPDS No. 52-1008), indicating co-existence of NiSe and Co0.85Se with no impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows XRD pattern of NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF... All the diffraction peaks can be ascribed to the hexagonal NiSe (JCPDS No. 02-0892) and hexagonal close-packed Co0.85Se (JCPDS No. 52-1008), indicating the co-existence of NiSe and Co0.85Se, and no impurities appeared in the composite.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co0.85Se and NiSe formed dendritic nanoarrays on NF surface, which could not be separated even after long-term sonication.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figures 2b, c and S4 show the different magnified SEM and TEM images of NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF. The Co0.85Se and NiSe formed the dendritic nanoarrays on the surface of NF, which could not be separated even after long-term sonication...

nodes.characterization_summary: Dendritic nanoarrays of Co0.85Se and NiSe well integrated on NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figures 2b, c and S4 show the different magnified SEM and TEM images of NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe (100) plane at 0.32 nm and Co0.85Se (101) facet at 0.27 nm lattice distances confirm well-integrated heterointerfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The heterointerfaces were further characterized by high resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), as shown in Fig. 2d. Obviously, NiSe... and Co0.85Se... were well integrated. The displayed lattice distances of 0.32 and 0.27 nm are in accordance with the (100) plane of NiSe and (101) facet of Co0.85Se, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni, Co, and Se evenly distributed in NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF bulk.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping images (Fig. 2e) indicated that Ni (green), Co (yellow) and Se (red) evenly distributed in the bulk.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p3/2 peak shifts positively to 854.7 eV from 854.1 eV in NiSe/NF indicating Ni oxidation; Co 2p shows decreased Co3+ and increased Co2+ vs Co0.85Se indicating Co reduction due to electron transfer from NiSe to Co0.85Se domains.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high resolution of the Ni 2p (Fig. 3b) spectra shows that the Ni 2p3/2 peak in NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF (854.7 eV) displays a positive shift compared to the NiSe/NF (854.1 eV), demonstrating the oxidation of Ni after forming the heterostructure... the peak intensity of Co3+ decreased while that of Co2+ increased in NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF, indicating the reduction of average valence state of Co

nodes.characterization_summary: Valence band positions: NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF at 3.01 eV, NiSe/NF at 3.7 eV, Co0.85Se/NF at 4.40 eV; smaller valence band of composite confirms enhanced electronic conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results show that the valence bands of NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF, NiSe/NF and Co0.85Se/NF are 3.01, 3.7 and 4.40 eV, respectively. The smaller valence band structure of NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF confirmed its significantly enhanced electronic conductivity

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance (Cdl) of NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF is much higher than NiSe/NF and Co0.85Se/NF, demonstrating more catalytic active sites from heterogeneous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the double layer capacitance (Cdl) was performed to calculate the electrochemical active surface area (ECSA)... The Cdl of NiSe@Co0.85Se/NF catalyst is much higher than those of NiSe/NF and Co0.85Se/NF, demonstrating that the heterogeneous structure... can introduce more catalytic active sites
